method.classifier: scripts/p020_exec_classify.py load_model, select_model_optimization, and classify_batch, prepared as classify_all; every frame paired with its previous frame (sample rate 1)
method.gpu_samples: nvidia-smi on every GPU every 500 ms, labeled with the phase on arrival and 1000 ms earlier
method.operating_point: fastest Tetris test configuration with HOTA >= reference HOTA x (1 - 0.05) (common.fastest_tetris)
method.order: per video: decode, rgb_copy, classifier, classifier_1, classifier_stream, detector, detector_16, on the same decoded frames
method.placement: CPU affinity and memory bound to the GPU's NUMA node (numactl --cpunodebind --membind), checked at start; anonymous pages per node recorded per video

runs.classifier: p020's classify_batch, 16 consecutive frames per call (p020's batching)
runs.classifier_stream: classify_batch over the video in 16-frame calls, synchronized only before the first and after the last call (one interval), as p020 runs
runs.decode: cv2 decoding of the whole video to BGR frames (one interval)
runs.detector: polyis.models.detector.detect, one BGR frame per call (p002, batch size 1)
runs.detector_16: polyis.models.detector.detect_batch, 16 consecutive BGR frames per call
runs.rgb_copy: p020's BGR-to-RGB contiguous copy of every frame (one interval; Tetris only, untimed in p121)

method.timing: torch.cuda.synchronize() before and after every timed call; time.perf_counter_ns; a call's time split evenly over its frames. Per-call synchronization removes p020's overlap of host work with the previous batch's GPU tail, so the per-call classifier runs are an upper bound on its steady-state cost; classifier_stream synchronizes once per video
method.videos: 3 test videos per dataset, evenly spaced in name order, every frame
method.warmup: untimed: every run over the first video, the detector runs on its first 32 frames only
